question: Over the five parallel 2-CEES adsorption experiments with FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs, what is the mean mass gain, and what adsorption capacity in mg/g does it give?
rendered:
To calculate the mean mass gain, add the five mass gains and divide by 5. 

The mass gains are: 
8.7 mg, 7.8 mg, 8.1 mg, 7.9 mg, 8.4 mg.

The mean mass gain is: 
(8.7 + 7.8 + 8.1 + 7.9 + 8.4) / 5 = 8.04 mg

The mass before adsorption was 5 mg in all experiments. 
The mean mass gain is 8.04 mg, so the mean mass after adsorption is 5 + 8.04 = 13.04 mg.

The mean adsorption capacity is the mean mass gain divided by the mass of the sample before adsorption (5 mg) multiplied by 1000 (to convert from mg to g). 
13.04 mg / 5 mg * 1000 = 261.6 mg/g.

However, the text states that the average apparent adsorption capacity of FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs is 636 mg g^−1.
